reviewed_contracts.assessment: The dedicated worker waits for the exact spawned kqprun PID using wait4. Parent recipe/schema construction, row decoding and independent oracles are outside that child accounting. Startup, schema, fixtures, compilation, target execution and kernel-attributed waited descendants remain included.

Existing rbo-direct cgroup is required and wrapper membership rechecked. start_new_session creates a private process group without creating another cgroup or systemd scope. Only original payload fds reach kqprun; report/source fds are not in target pass_fds. Caller owns payload fds; integration owns and closes only its fresh wrapper/report fds.

Normal worker execution reaps the exact target and communicates its terminal status; caller reaps the worker and checks the private group is empty. Timeout/cancellation kill the owned private group and bound drain/reap. After group-wide fatal termination, the outer cgroup remains responsible for remaining/reparented descendants; local drain alone is not treated as whole-scope proof. Only one selected cell can run, and outer guard failure rejects its observation.

Retains source/generator/dependency/workload identities, sample coordinates, actual revision and executable/build-receipt identity, UDF/environment/affinity/cgroup bindings and sealed nonce-bound report hash. Post-oracle source and runner provenance checks remain. Guard evidence path/hash and final cleanup are attached independently; the raw record stays non-accepting.

Kernel lifetime ru_maxrss is converted from KiB to bytes and is not a target-only peak or summed cgroup peak. Existing 24 GiB scope/36 GiB host headroom, output guards and scope cleanup remain. No scaling threshold, speedup claim, matrix completion or accepting resource validator is introduced.
